hypothesis: tomoe (3-fold comma, deliberately asymmetric) survives lattice folding BETTER than the highly symmetric mon
why: Asymmetry is not the operative variable and cannot be, because fractal() computes `vec2 uv = abs(p)` BEFORE the cell distance - a 4-fold mirror on the sampling coordinate. Any chiral motif is symmetrised: the comma is never drawn as a comma, only as a mirrored comma PAIR forming an achiral leaf (see tomoe-chirality-sheet.png). What actually decides how much a motif restyles the lattice is BOUNDARY CROSSINGS PER RADIAL DIRECTION - how many times a ray from the cell centre crosses the silhouette inside the sampled annulus. tomoe is one convex blob plus one thin tail, so most rays cross once and abs(cellD-gRingGap) yields a single ring, nearly the hexagon's own topology: only 42.3% of pixels differ from the hex baseline at t=8. ume (5-fold, SYMMETRIC, 5 lobes + deep notches = many crossings per ray) differs by 91.4%. kikko differs by 46.6% but is confounded - kikko IS a hexagon. So the symmetric mon beat the asymmetric one on the very metric the hypothesis claimed for it.
next: Rank the remaining mon by radial boundary-crossing count (lobes+notches), not by symmetry or fold count; kiku (12 lobes) should top it. If chirality is ever wanted on the wall, `uv = abs(p)` is the line to change - but it is load-bearing fold geometry, so that is its own experiment.
spawned: `uv = abs(p)` in fractal() destroys all motif chirality by construction - is a chirality-preserving fold (e.g. fold on one axis only) worth the geometry risk?

HANDOFF s5 fact 3 is misleading as written: UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL=true PREVENTS the flip rather than causing one; the bake needs no Y compensation (proved by tomoe-probe.frag). Worth correcting in the doc before teammates 'fix' a bake that is already right.
Lit area does NOT drop for tomoe (12.20 -> 12.71 meanLum, 6.4% -> 7.2% lit): the predicted darkening is motif-dependent, not universal, so a blanket counter-ratchet would over-brighten.
ume at BEAD_MIX=1 is the most visually striking cell tested (bold red/blue rosettes) - it deserves its own /lab run as a keeper candidate.
